result.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
result.summary: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Cross-Interface Policy Regularization（CIPR）：把动作名替换为无信息标识符，并将同一训练样本以两种语义等价的接口呈现，用两组动作分布之间的 KL 散度作为自监督正则，使 LLM agent 的策略在接口变化下保持一致；在监督与强化学习后训练中均提升了接口扰动下的鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「语义等价输入应诱导一致内部决策」的正则化思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节扰动下 latent 推理状态是否稳定的训练与贡献分配设计；但该文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，需人工判断迁移可行性。
